summary: One blocking safety-display race remains. Cutoff handling, diagnostic specification, and adherence tests are resolved. Findings use source inspection, saved-result recalculation, and in-memory probes; full application tests, browser testing, and new Stan fits were not run.

prior_points.comment: Pilot and confirmatory collection remain clearly separated, with cutoff enforcement corrected.
Whole-day weather and evening context remain explicit contemporaneous adjustment exceptions.
Weather collection stops at yesterday in the participant's time zone.
Potential bias in average mood and associations from outcome-dependent nonresponse remains acknowledged.
Binary contrasts replace observed or imputed contributions with predictions at yes and no.
Convergence requirements, private warnings, confirmatory reruns, and publication gating remain implemented or specified.
Evidence categories are computed before probabilities are rounded.
Simulated outcomes use rounded covariates, and true effects use each replicate's fitted standard deviations.
Both opt-in recovery tests check effect detection and divergent transitions; they were not rerun.
Evening forms save edited fields only, preserving intervening automatic updates.
Device submissions retain acknowledgment-only responses, including duplicate reports.
Nested publication fields remain explicitly constructed and covered by the adversarial-field test.
Backup retention and push-service metadata disclosures remain accurate.
Both adherence measures count begun slots; fixed-time probes confirmed their denominators.
Private-study ethics rationale and prospective reassessment remain explicit.
Previously corrected expressed-mood rhythm statement and citation remain unchanged.
Other screen time and social media have distinct estimands, with fallback analyses specified.
Independent-imputation limitations and temporally informed, type-appropriate sensitivity analysis remain specified.
Slot restriction, informative-nonresponse sensitivity, and reminder-response definition remain explicit.
Recalculated CSV summaries match reported results; convergence and unsimulated-remediation limitations remain explicit.
Threshold-specific diagnostics now specify the model, comparison criterion, and reporting response.
Source filtering, overlap checks, monitor placement, and proprietary HRV limitations remain explicit.
Prospective experiment amendments retain design, estimand, adherence, carryover, and reporting requirements.
Routine safety refresh paths are implemented, but a stale response can hide an active notice; see M25.
Early stopping permits confirmatory analysis and requires reporting its date and reason.
Identifiable disclosure, inference across updates, and withdrawal limits remain acknowledged.
Reporting checklist retains the distinction between observational requirements and future experiments.
Conditional latent dynamics remain distinguished from observed mood variability.
Search details, device scope, and affiliations remain specified; exact record count was not independently reproduced.
Publication rereads the cutoff immediately before writing. Refits share one cutoff, waiting runs record it, and Trends suppresses stale tags. In-memory transition probes passed.
Idempotent migration retains study_start and preserves existing records.
Ultrahuman responses require the requested date, and current-day steps remain excluded.
Predictive checks use central 95% intervals, classify failures before rounding, and display failure markers and counts.
Deterministic contrast test covers observed yes, observed no, missing flags, and continuous shifts.
Submission, queue, resume, and reconnect paths pass ordinary in-memory checks. A new response-ordering race can reverse the notice; see M25.

Likelihood, coefficient priors, and joint ordering restriction now address the crossing concern described in the [VGAM documentation](https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/VGAM/html/cumulative.html). Diagnostic implementation is explicitly due before six months.
Fixed morning and afternoon tests assert both adherence measures and distinguish the former incorrect denominator.

must_fix.problem: A delayed safety refresh can overwrite a newer report's safety state. Executing the actual client script in memory reproduced this sequence: resume starts a refresh returning false; a subsequent threshold-crossing report shows the notice; the delayed false response hides it. The empty-queue timer does not restore the notice.
must_fix.requested_change: Serialize safety refresh with report delivery or reject obsolete responses. Add a client regression test that delivers the older false response after the newer true response and verifies that the notice stays visible.
